description: Progressive MSA followed by MUSCLE-style tree-dependent restricted-partitioning refinement (Edgar 2004, stage 3): each guide-tree edge splits the alignment into two profiles that are re-aligned and kept only if the sum-of-pairs score strictly improves; repeated until convergence or maxIterations passes. The result's sum-of-pairs score is never below multiple_align_progressive's. Default linear gap model (gapOpen ignored); gapModel='affine' refines under the natural affine sum-of-pairs objective with the affine profile DP. distance='clustalw' selects ClustalW 2.1's pairwise stage for the guide tree and guideTree='nj' neighbour-joining (see multiple_align_progressive); the refinement partitions are the edges of that tree. PROTEIN / MATRIX: type='protein' (or matrix) refines under the matrix sum-of-pairs objective (see multiple_align_progressive); rows equal an independent Python implementation. With type='protein', distance='clustalw' / 'clustalw-quick' use ClustalW 2.1's PROTEIN pairwise stages (GONNET250 / BLOSUM30 / PAM350 / identity matrix via pwMatrix, gap 10 / 0.1, k-tuple 1; exact ports verified on 4 204 + 3 774 pairs of clustalw -TYPE=PROTEIN -ALIGN / -QUICKTREE).

sequences.description: Sequences to align (at least one): DNA (A, C, G, T) by default, amino acids with type='protein'.

gapOpen.description: Gap-open penalty. Used only with gapModel='affine' (a gap of length k then costs gapOpen + k * gapExtend, Gotoh); ignored by the default linear model. May be fractional only with a substitution matrix (type='protein' or matrix).

gapExtend.description: Gap penalty per gap position (linear model: every gap position; affine model: the per-position part of gapOpen + k * gapExtend). May be fractional (e.g. -0.5) only with a substitution matrix (type='protein' or matrix).

maxIterations.description: Upper bound on full refinement passes (>= 1).

distance.description: Guide-tree distance: 'linear' (default) = 1 - identities / min(length) of the repository's global alignment under the given scores (linear NW, or Gotoh when gapModel='affine'); 'clustalw' = the same formula on ClustalW 2.1's own pairwise stage (affine local Smith-Waterman-Gotoh alignment with its IUB matrix x100 and gap penalties 15 / 6.66, the 'slow' full-DP mode of clustalw -ALIGN; type='protein': its PROTEIN stage with the GONNET250 / BLOSUM30 / PAM350 / identity matrix (pwMatrix) and gap penalties 10 / 0.1 (pwGapOpen / pwGapExtend); the match/mismatch/gap parameters are then used only for the profile alignment); 'clustalw-quick' = ClustalW 2.1's fast k-tuple mode (clustalw -QUICKTREE, FastPairwiseAlign.cpp: best chain of exactly matching k-mers on the top diagonals, d = (100 - 100*fragmentScore/min(length))/100; tuned by ktuple / window / topDiagonals / pairGap).

gapModel.description: 'linear' (default): every gap position costs gapExtend and gapOpen is ignored; totalScore is the column sum of pairs (gap-gap columns 0). 'affine': gap runs cost gapOpen + k * gapExtend; the pairwise / profile alignments use affine (Gotoh) dynamic programming and totalScore is the sum of pairs with natural affine gap costs (Altschul 1989: each pair of rows is projected out of the alignment, gap-gap columns skipped, every gap run of the projection pays gapOpen once). For two sequences the affine result is an optimal pairwise alignment; for three or more sequences every method is a heuristic.

guideTree.description: Guide-tree method: 'upgma' (default; Sokal & Michener 1958, the Feng-Doolittle / CLUSTAL-1 choice) or 'nj' (neighbour-joining, Saitou & Nei 1987 - ClustalW 2.1's default tree, T-Coffee/Clustal-style; the unrooted NJ tree is rooted and ordered exactly as clustalw does: Tree::reRoot, left subtree first). With distance='clustalw' and guideTree='nj' the tree equals the .dnd file of clustalw -ALIGN. UPGMA is built by the canonical phylogenetics builder; NJ uses ClustalW's own neighbour-joining arithmetic (exact ties as in clustalw).

ktuple.description: distance='clustalw-quick' only: k-tuple (word) size, 1-4 for DNA (clustalw -KTUPLE, default 2), 1-2 for protein (default 1).

window.description: distance='clustalw-quick' only: diagonals scanned around each top diagonal (clustalw -WINDOW, default 4 for DNA, 5 for protein).

topDiagonals.description: distance='clustalw-quick' only: number of best diagonals used (clustalw -TOPDIAGS, default 4 for DNA, 5 for protein).

pairGap.description: distance='clustalw-quick' only: gap penalty of the fragment chain (clustalw -PAIRGAP; DNA default 5, or ktuple + 4 when ktuple is given; protein default 3, or ktuple + 3, as the clustalw command line does).

type.description: Sequence type: 'dna' (default; A, C, G, T scored with match/mismatch) or 'protein' (amino-acid sequences scored with the substitution matrix, default BLOSUM62; match/mismatch are then ignored). The protein path shares the dynamic programs, merge, profile and objective code of the DNA path (no second implementation).

matrix.description: Optional substitution matrix: BLOSUM62 or PAM250 (type='protein'), EDNAFULL (IUPAC DNA, type='dna'). When given (or type='protein'), match/mismatch are ignored, residues are scored by the published table (case-insensitive, any symbol of the matrix), gapOpen/gapExtend may be fractional (EMBOSS needle numbers gapopen G / gapextend E = gapOpen -(G - E), gapExtend -E) and the result also carries the real-valued exactTotalScore (totalScore = rounded). Verified against independent Python implementations of every method, Biopython 1.88 pairwise optima and exhaustive enumeration of tiny sets.

pwMatrix.description: type='protein' with distance='clustalw': ClustalW's pairwise matrix (clustalw -PWMATRIX): 'gonnet' (default; GONNET250), 'blosum' (BLOSUM30), 'pam' (PAM350) or 'id' (identity).

pwGapOpen.description: type='protein' with distance='clustalw': ClustalW -PWGAPOPEN (default 10; length-dependent: 2 * matrixAvg * (open + ln min(length)) in matrix units).

alignedSequences.description: The aligned rows of the MSA.

consensus.description: Majority-vote consensus of the aligned rows (gaps vote; a nucleotide beats a gap on ties).

totalScore.description: Sum-of-pairs score of the MSA: linear model = column score (match/mismatch from the matrix, residue-gap = gapExtend, gap-gap = 0); gapModel='affine' = natural affine gap costs (every gap run of each pair projection pays gapOpen once).

exactTotalScore.description: Real-valued sum-of-pairs score (= totalScore for DNA with integer scores; the exact score, e.g. 49.5, for substitution-matrix runs with fractional gaps, where totalScore is rounded half away from zero).
